title: Cursor Page
statement: Implement `solve(ids, cursor, limit)`. Sort `ids` ascending. `cursor` is the empty string for the first page, or an id from the list. Return `{"ids": page, "next": last_id or ""}`. `next` is empty when the page is short or there is nothing after it. `limit` outside 1 through 100 returns `error`. An unknown cursor returns `error`.
hints: Find the start just after the cursor, or 0 when the cursor is empty.
The page is the next limit ids. next is the last id only when more remain.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: A cursor that means the last id you returned, plus a stable sort, does not skip or duplicate rows when new ids are inserted above the cursor.

editorial: A cursor that means the last id you returned, plus a stable sort, does not skip or duplicate rows when new ids are inserted above the cursor. Offset pages do. The empty next string tells the client to stop.
